passage:
Sunday night.
This week I sent 300 applications. Same CV, same cover note, name of company pasted in. I felt busy all week and thought that had to count for something.
The numbers: four automatic replies, two polite rejections, one phone call. In that call the recruiter asked why I wanted "this particular role", and I couldn't remember which company it was.
Zeenat rang and asked how it was going. I said "fine". Zeenat said three careful ones beat a hundred blind ones, and I snapped back that it wasn't helping.
Now I feel worse than on Monday. All that clicking, and nothing to show for it.
Don't know what to do tomorrow.
— Gurpreet

qa.q: How does Gurpreet feel at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Gurpreet feels worse and lost, saying so directly, and is unsure what to do next.

qa.q: What could Gurpreet try instead of sending hundreds of the same application?
qa.a: Gurpreet could pick a few roles, match the CV to each listing and mention something specific about each company.

qa.q: How might Zeenat have felt after Gurpreet snapped back?
qa.a: Zeenat was probably concerned and a little hurt, wanting to help but getting a sharp answer.

grounding: The diary shows a laid-off developer sending hundreds of identical applications in a week, getting few replies and feeling worse while mistaking clicking for progress.

passage:
After the layoff, Karthik moved back to his parents' house in a small town near Tiruvannamalai to save on rent. The internet only worked properly on the terrace, so every night he sat up there under the stars with his laptop and hit "apply" on job portals: fifty, a hundred, by Sunday three hundred. Same CV, same line: "I am interested in this opportunity."
Nitin, his school friend who ran the mobile shop on the main road, came up with two glasses of tea on Monday. "How many interviews?"
"None yet. Two automated no's."
"Three hundred and none?"
Karthik shrugged. "It's a numbers game."
But at dinner he barely ate, and Amma noticed. He had done more than ever and felt more useless than ever. On the terrace that night he scrolled the list of companies and couldn't remember what half of them did.

qa.q: Where did the internet work properly?
How did Karthik feel after three hundred applications?
qa.a: He felt more useless than ever, low enough to barely eat at dinner.
Choose a small number of roles he really wants, learn what those companies do, and tailor his CV and message to each.

qa.a: Amma noticed him barely eating and was probably worried about how the search was weighing on him.

grounding: It shows a laid-off developer sending three hundred identical applications, getting almost no replies and feeling worse, mistaking activity for progress.
